raw_case_text:
At the time of the referral, the patient was 12 years old and living in Pretoria with her aunt. Her mother lived in Limpopo and was also using ART. The patient was aware of her HIV status and it was known to all her close adult family members. She reported poor adherence with her ART treatment because it was unpalatable.
She had three genotypic drug resistance tests (DRTs) over the next 2 years and the mutations evolved from low-level resistance to ritonavir-boosted lopinavir to extensive three-class resistance during this time (Table 1). She moved again to a private general practitioner in 2012 where she had another DRT performed at a private laboratory which confirmed the results of the second test. She was then changed to third-line therapy consisting of tenofovir (TDF), emtricitabine (FTC), ritonavir-boosted darunavir, raltegravir (RAL) and etravirine. The ARVs were delivered monthly from June 2012 to February 2015 by courier pharmacy and no parcels were returned. She attended all monitoring visits and initially had an excellent response to the third-line regimen.
However, by 2013 the patient was not coping well and had developed urinary and faecal incontinence without a physiological cause. She had nearly been raped, had failed grade 9 and had become socially isolated. By December 2013, her viral load reflected the impact of the psychological problems on her adherence. Her mother passed away in 2015 and with that the patient lost her medical aid benefits and was referred back to the state sector. A fourth DRT (Table 1) showed that resistance to the non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors and protease inhibitors had worsened and also now included resistance to the integrase strand transfer inhibitors (INSTIs).
Currently, neither the patient nor the family seem to have grasped the seriousness of her condition. Despite multiple adherence counselling sessions and even contracting with the family that her pill-taking will be supervised, there is still inadequate supervision. She has poor coping skills, has not entirely accepted her illness and is ambivalent about taking her ART. She is now on a holding regimen consisting of FTC, TDF, AZT and abacavir (ABC). A tropism assay predicted that CCR5-antagonists are likely to be effective.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 12-year-old female presenting for management of perinatally acquired retroviral disease and multidrug-resistant virologic treatment failure.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented following referral for complex antiretroviral management due to persistent medication non-adherence driven by taste aversion. Over a two-year period, serial genotypic resistance assays demonstrated progression from single-class resistance to extensive three-class drug resistance. Although she initially showed virologic response to third-line salvage therapy initiated in 2012, severe psychosocial trauma (including an attempted sexual assault, academic failure, and the death of her mother in 2015) led to social isolation, non-physiological urinary and fecal incontinence, and severe treatment default culminating in four-class antiretroviral resistance.
subjective.past_medical_history: Perinatally acquired human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection; maternal HIV infection on ART (deceased in 2015); history of poor adherence to first- and second-line antiretroviral regimens due to medication unpalatability; no underlying structural genitourinary or gastrointestinal pathology.
subjective.review_of_systems: Psychogenic urinary and fecal incontinence, social withdrawal, emotional distress; denies chronic fever, opportunistic infections, respiratory distress, or localized pain.

objective.physical_examination: Adolescent female in stable general physical condition; absence of physiological causes for urinary or fecal incontinence; normal cardiopulmonary, abdominal, and neurological examinations.
objective.advanced_workup: Serial genotypic drug resistance testing (DRT): DRT 1-3 demonstrated progressive development of high-level resistance to nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs), non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs), and ritonavir-boosted protease inhibitors (PIs). Fourth DRT demonstrated extensive cross-class resistance including emerging resistance to integrase strand transfer inhibitors (INSTIs). Viral tropism assay: Predicted functional coreceptor tropism with likelihood of response to CCR5-antagonists (maraviroc).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Perinatally acquired human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection complicated by multiclass drug resistance (pan-resistant to NRTIs, NNRTIs, PIs, and INSTIs) secondary to severe psychosocial trauma, grief, and treatment non-adherence, presenting with functional/psychogenic encopresis and enuresis.
Plan & Outcome: Placed on an interim nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor holding regimen comprising tenofovir (TDF), emtricitabine (FTC), zidovudine (AZT), and abacavir (ABC) to maintain replicative fitness impairment while salvage regimens are formulated. Initiated intensive multidisciplinary adolescent adherence counseling, psychological support, social services involvement, and directly observed therapy agreements with family caregivers, with future consideration of CCR5 coreceptor antagonist-based regimens.
